title: An integral tensor pair coprime modulo an ideal becomes coprime on an etale neighbourhood
statement: Let $A,B,C$ be commutative rings, with $A$-algebra structures on $B$ and $C$, and suppose $B$ is integral over $A$. Let $I\subseteq C$ be an ideal and put $S=B\otimes_A C$. Let $x,z\in S$ have coprime images in $S/IS$, meaning that these two images admit a Bezout identity. Then there exist a commutative ring $D$ and a ring map $\psi:C\to D$ such that $\operatorname{Spec} D\to\operatorname{Spec} C$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], the canonical map $C/I\to D/ID$ is bijective, and the images of $x,z$ under $b\otimes c\mapsto b\otimes\psi(c)$ are coprime in $B\otimes_A D$. The $A$-algebra structure on $D$ is the composite of $A\to C$ and $\psi$.

proof.text: Put $S=B\otimes_A C$ and let $\iota:C\to S$ send $c$ to $1\otimes c$. This ring map is integral by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-base-change], transporting along the tensor commutor. Put $J=(x,z)$ and $K=IS$. Choose lifts $u,v\in S$ of the coefficients of a Bezout identity in $S/K$. Then $w=1-(ux+vz)\in K$.

The image of $V(J)$ in $\operatorname{Spec} C$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-spec-closed-map]. It misses $V(I)$: if a prime $\mathfrak p$ of $S$ contains $J$ and its inverse image contains $I$, then $K\subseteq\mathfrak p$, so both $w$ and $ux+vz$ belong to $\mathfrak p$, forcing $1\in\mathfrak p$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-separate-image-closed-from-closed] to obtain $a\in C$ with $a\equiv1\pmod I$ and $\iota(a)\in J$.

Take $D=C[a^{-1}]$ and let $\psi:C\to D$ be its localization map. Its spectrum map is an open immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Since $a\bmod I=1$, localization has a map $\tau:D\to C/I$ extending the quotient map. The ideal $ID$ lies in its kernel, so it factors through $D/ID$. This factorization is inverse to $C/I\to D/ID$: one composite is the identity on the representatives $c\bmod I$; the other is the identity after precomposition with $C\to D$, hence is the identity by uniqueness of a localization map. Thus the canonical quotient map is bijective.

Let $m:S\to B\otimes_A D$ be induced by $b\otimes c\mapsto b\otimes\psi(c)$. Write $\iota(a)=rx+sz$. Its image under $m$ equals $1\otimes\psi(a)$ and is a unit. If $t$ is its inverse, then $(t\,m(r))m(x)+(t\,m(s))m(z)=1$. This is the desired coprimality. The equalities on tensor factors follow from the universal property of the tensor product.
